system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

content.text:
# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: AWS
G2: GCP
G3: software development
G4: Go beyond terratest

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Filling the 2020-2022 or 2024 gaps with invented jobs or stretching neighbouring date ranges
T2: Disclosing more private/medical detail than needed (father's death) instead of a neutral 'career break' if anything
T3: Claiming AWS or GCP for multi-cloud ads
T4: Calling him a software developer or claiming Python/Go development
T5: Old cover letter targets an IT Administrator job and says 'available to start immediately' - no longer true
T6: The CV lists skills first; writer should keep dates accurate when reordering

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Samuel Achterberg-Osei
Cloud & Infrastructure Engineer
Rotterdam, Netherlands | samuel.ao@example.com | +31 6 5555 0707
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud and infrastructure engineer with hands-on experience designing, building and operating Azure
environments. Focused on Terraform-based infrastructure, cloud networking, cloud environment design
and operation, and deployment automation. Experienced in operating large Windows and Linux server
estates, leading infrastructure delivery, automating deployments, and supporting AKS operations.
CORE SKILLS
Cloud: Microsoft Azure (VMs, VNets, App Service, AKS, Azure Migrate)
Infrastructure as Code: Terraform; Terratest module tests
Cloud operations: Azure DevOps YAML pipelines, Kubernetes (AKS), Docker, Helm
Networking, security and access: Hub-spoke networks, Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private
endpoints, VNet peering, TCP/IP, DNS, VPN, site-to-site VPN, firewalls, MFA, Conditional Access
Systems and automation: Windows Server, Linux (Ubuntu, RHEL), Active Directory / Entra ID,
Microsoft 365 administration, PowerShell, Bash
EXPERIENCE
Cloud Engineer (Contract) | Havenstad Logistics B.V., Rotterdam Mar 2025 – Present
• Part of a three-person cloud team operating an Azure estate of approximately 400 VMs and 12 AKS
clusters across three subscriptions.
• Designed and built reusable Terraform modules for hub-spoke landing-zone networking, including
Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints for storage and SQL, and VNet peering across
subscriptions.
• Added Terratest module tests to the pipeline and implemented a nightly infrastructure
drift-detection job.
• Replaced manual deployments for 15 internal .NET and Node applications with Azure DevOps
YAML pipelines for build, test and deployment to App Service or AKS. Deployment frequency
increased from roughly monthly to several times per week for most applications.
• Supported AKS operations, including upgrades, node pools and ingress; development teams own
application manifests.
Freelance IT Administrator | Self-employed, small businesses Sep 2022 – Jan 2024
• Set up and supported Microsoft 365 and Azure AD for nine small businesses with 5–40 employees.
• Migrated two clients from on-premises file servers to SharePoint and OneDrive.
• Created a repeatable PowerShell script and checklist for security baselines, including MFA,
Conditional Access, mailbox auditing and backups.
Systems Administrator | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services, Schiedam Jan 2014 – Feb 2020
• Administered approximately 250 Windows and Linux servers supporting municipal services.
• Led the technical delivery of a lift-and-shift migration of 60 VMware servers to Azure IaaS using
Azure Migrate, Azure VMs, VNets and site-to-site VPN; completed cutover over six weekends with
no unplanned downtime.
• Automated user provisioning and patch reporting with PowerShell.
• Served as second-line escalation for network and Active Directory issues.
Helpdesk Technician | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services Aug 2011 – Dec 2013
CAREER BREAKS AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
Mar 2020 – Aug 2022 | Full-time family caregiving; maintained Azure Administrator knowledge and
provided unpaid IT support to church and family.
Feb 2024 – Feb 2025 | Completed a part-time, online, three-month English-language cloud bootcamp
(Dec 2024); studied Terraform and built a Proxmox homelab.
EDUCATION
MBO 4 IT Systems and Networks | Delta Vocational College, 2011
CERTIFICATIONS
Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104), 2019
HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate (003), 2025
LANGUAGES
Dutch (native) | English (fluent) | Twi (spoken)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role on the Fleet
Connectivity team. I bring hands-on experience designing and operating Azure infrastructure,
building Terraform-based networking, and improving deployment automation. Corvale’s work
to shape the cloud platform for its new train fleet is a compelling opportunity to apply that
experience to infrastructure being built for production from the start.
In my current contract, I am part of a three-person cloud team operating an Azure estate of
approximately 400 virtual machines and 12 AKS clusters. I designed reusable Terraform
modules for hub-and-spoke networking across three subscriptions, including Azure Firewall,
private DNS zones, private endpoints and VNet peering. I also added Terraform module tests
and a nightly infrastructure drift-detection job, and replaced manual deployments for 15
applications with Azure DevOps pipelines. These projects have strengthened my focus on
infrastructure that is maintainable, testable and reliable in operation.
Earlier, as a systems administrator for municipal services, I led the technical delivery of a
migration of 60 VMware servers to Azure IaaS. The cutover was completed over six weekends
without unplanned downtime. My experience also includes network and Active Directory
escalation, site-to-site VPNs, and practical security work such as implementing MFA and
Conditional Access for small businesses. I hold the Azure Administrator Associate and
Terraform Associate certifications.
That work required leading the technical delivery from planning through cutover and
coordinating the infrastructure changes needed to keep municipal services available.
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my cloud infrastructure, networking,
systems-design and automation experience could support Corvale’s fleet connectivity platform
and its engineering-led, collaborative approach to owning systems end to end.
Kind regards,
Samuel Achterberg-Osei

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
